data.narrative:
INTALUS is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $31M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a broader peer universe of nine private robotics firms and one public comparable (277810.KQ), though narrow-stage peer data is limited within this sector.

The Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable approach, using the $31M total raised as a proxy for current valuation and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $78M. A Peer-Median triangulation was not executable: while ten same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, only one operates at the same stage, and filtering for adjacent-stage or similar-tier comparables yielded insufficient datapoints (fewer than three) to derive a reliable median. Relying on an all-sector median would introduce material distortion given heterogeneity in robotics subsectors and capital intensity.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $66M (low) to $89M (high), centered on $78M, based solely on stage-progression mechanics applied to deployed capital. Key uncertainties include the absence of same-stage peer density necessary for market-rate validation and the company's position within the robotics subsector taxonomy. Any refinement would require either disclosure of near-peer financing rounds or clarification of INTALUS's specific vertical and technology readiness level relative to the ten identified comparables.
